key_insight: Explicitly modeling inter-object occlusions in 3D layout-conditioned text-to-image generation produces depth-consistent, scale-correct images that accurately render partially occluded objects.
problem_solved: Existing layout-conditioned generators often ignore precise occlusion relationships, producing images with incorrect depth ordering, object scale, and unrealistic partial occlusions; SeeThrough3D addresses accurate occlusion reasoning for realistic compositional scene synthesis.
method: Introduce an occlusion-aware 3D scene representation that encodes object depth, masks, and visibility relationships to guide image synthesis.

Integrate occlusion reasoning into the generative pipeline (e.g., conditioning a diffusion/model decoder on depth+visibility cues or using a differentiable occlusion module) so generated pixels respect inter-object depth and partial occlusion.
Train with occlusion-sensitive losses and paired supervision (layout, depth/masks, target image) plus qualitative consistency checks to enforce scale and geometry fidelity.
impact: Improves controllability and realism for multi-object scene generation, enabling reliable synthesis of partially occluded objects for applications in AR/VR, content creation, and data generation for downstream vision tasks.

paper_title: SeeThrough3D: Occlusion Aware 3D Control in Text-to-Image Generation
paper_authors: Vaibhav Agrawal, Rishubh Parihar, Pradhaan Bhat, Ravi Kiran Sarvadevabhatla, R. Venkatesh Babu
